transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah. I guess mostly I came in because my sleep’s been pretty bad. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I’ll lie there for hours sometimes, especially if I hear rain, or I start thinking about the bluff giving way. Then when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up sweaty from dreams and I go into the call center feeling like I didn’t sleep at all. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Can you tell me a bit more about what you mean when you say 'the bluff giving way'? Does it remind you of a specific event or experience?

Yeah… um, it was on a trail. I don’t really like talking about it too much, but the bluff sort of came apart, I guess. And now sometimes stuff just pops into my head out of nowhere—like the sound of rocks sliding, or my leg being stuck under me.

It’s not like I’m trying to think about it. I’ll be at my desk with my headset on, and for a minute it feels like I’m back there instead of at work. I don’t know if that makes sense.
Have you noticed yourself feeling more down or hopeless lately, like a weight that doesn’t go away?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it hopeless exactly. It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult or anything.

Most days there’s just this… scared feeling underneath everything. And I feel embarrassed, like people can tell I messed up somehow, or that I’m not as tough as I used to act. I know that probably sounds kind of dumb, but it’s there a lot.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends?

Um… I don’t know. I haven’t really thought of it that way, I guess.

I still… I mean, if someone asks me to do something, I’ll usually say yes. I don’t want people thinking I’m blowing them off. But I guess I’m not really the one making plans much lately. It’s not like I don’t like my friends or anything. I’m just kind of tired, maybe.

Is that what you mean?
Have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of what happened on the trail?

Yeah… I guess I do, a little. I mean, not like I’m trying to make a big thing out of it.

I just don’t really go near those coast trails anymore. If someone brings it up, I’ll kind of change the subject. And my old hiking buddies still text sometimes, but I… I don’t always answer right away. Sometimes I just don’t answer, honestly.

Even just talking about going back out there makes my chest get tight, so I kind of avoid it. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling more irritable, angry, or on edge lately, especially since the incident on the trail?

Yeah… I guess I have been more on edge. I try not to take it out on people, but at work my patience is just… shorter than it used to be.

Like, customers will ask something kind of small, or complain, and I’ll feel myself getting irritated really fast. I’ve snapped a couple times, raised my voice more than I should’ve. My supervisor actually pulled me aside once, which was embarrassing.

I don’t mean to be like that. I’m not trying to be rude to people. It just comes out quicker lately, if that makes sense.
